achados.description: New InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions widens type: teamId?: number for all scopes instead of required only for scope:'team'. This defeats the discriminated union InsightsBookingServiceOptions and allows scope:'team' without teamId (or scope:'user'/'org' with extraneous teamId) to pass type-check. Constructor then does safeParse and silently sets this.options=null instead of throwing, so invalid calls return NOTHING_CONDITION (1=0) and empty results rather than a compile-time or runtime error, masking bugs.

Constructor swallows validation errors: `const validation = schema.safeParse(options); this.options = validation.success ? validation.data : null`. On schema failure it silently degrades to null -> buildAuthorizationConditions returns Prisma.sql`1=0`. No exception is thrown, violating fail-fast and making misconfiguration (e.g., missing teamId) appear as 'no data' instead of an error.

getBaseConditions() branches on truthiness of Prisma.Sql objects: `if (authConditions && filterConditions) else if (authConditions) else if (filterConditions) else NOTHING`. Prisma.Sql is always a truthy object (even NOTHING_CONDITION = sql`1=0`), so the `else if (filterConditions)` (auth-bypass path returning filter alone) and final `else` are dead code. The structure documents an insecure fallback: if authConditions were ever nullable (as getFilterConditions is), it would return unscoped filter-only SQL, bypassing authorization. It also shows incorrect null-check logic.

Removes findMany() encapsulation that guaranteed authorization: previously `where: {...findManyArgs.where, AND: [authConditions, filterConditions]}` forced callers through an AND-merged WhereInput. Replaced with getBaseConditions(): Prisma.Sql that callers must manually interpolate via `prisma.$queryRaw` WHERE ${baseConditions}` (as test does). No longer enforces AND with caller filters/where, allows forgetting the condition, using OR, or incorrect parentheses, opening lateral authorization bypass. Region 57-78 introduces this broken contract.

getBaseConditions uses truthiness (if (authConditions && filterConditions)) but authConditions is always a Prisma.Sql object (even NOTHING_CONDITION = Prisma.sql`1=0` is truthy). So the test collapses to if(filterConditions), else-if(filterConditions) is dead code and else return NOTHING_CONDITION is unreachable. The intended null-check should be filterConditions !== null (and should explicitly handle the NOTHING case). The branch structure masks logic errors and relies on SQL evaluation of 1=0 rather than JS short-circuit.

Constructor signature was widened from InsightsBookingServiceOptions (discriminated union requiring teamId when scope==='team') to InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions where teamId is optional for all scopes. Invalid team scope (missing teamId) now passes type-checking and is silently coerced to this.options = null via safeParse, causing getAuthorizationConditions() to return NOTHING_CONDITION (1=0) with no error. Previously this was a compile-time error; now it is a silent fail-closed that hides caller bugs.

Breaking contract: findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs) which merged findManyArgs.where via AND [authConditions, filterConditions] and forwarded select/orderBy/take/skip was removed and replaced by getBaseConditions(): Prisma.Sql requiring callers to do prisma.$queryRaw`WHERE ${baseConditions}`. Existing callers will get TypeError: findMany is not a function, and any caller-provided where/select/pagination is lost. Delegating raw SQL composition to callers also risks authorization bypass if they forget to interpolate WHERE ${baseConditions} or concatenate as string (SQL injection / over-broad reads).

Missing `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` but `getClient` uses `prisma.credential.update` at line 96. Results in ReferenceError: prisma is not defined at runtime on every Salesforce calendar operation, unlike every other CalendarService (googlecalendar, office365calendar) which imports prisma.

Success check is `response.statusText !== "OK"` instead of `!response.ok` / `response.status`. `statusText` is implementation-dependent (often "" in Node fetch) and not reliable; valid 200 with different text or paged fetch polyfill will incorrectly throw, and non-JSON error bodies are not handled via handleErrorsJson as other services do.

Updated tokens are persisted but never used for the returned connection: `new jsforce.Connection({ instanceUrl: credentialKey.instance_url, accessToken: credentialKey.access_token })` uses the stale `credentialKey` values instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.instance_url/access_token`. The current request therefore authenticates with the expired token even after a successful refresh.

Bypasses the `refreshOAuthTokens` wrapper used by all other services (googlecalendar, office365calendar, hubspot, lark, webex). When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, the fetch should go to the sync endpoint; this file always hits `login.salesforce.com` directly, breaking credential-sharing and diverging from `parseRefreshTokenResponse`'s minimum-schema branch.

Unconditional refresh on every `getClient()` call with no expiry check. Other services check `isExpired`/`isTokenExpiring` before refreshing; this causes a token refresh on every availability/event call, risking rate-limiting and unnecessary latency.

`salesforceTokenSchema` requires `scope: z.string()` (and `id`, `token_type` etc.) as required. Salesforce's `refresh_token` grant does not guarantee `scope` is returned; a valid refresh response lacking `scope` will fail `safeParse`, triggering "Invalid refreshed tokens" even though tokens are valid. Should be optional.

achados.description: Missing `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` in the header (lines 1-20). The PR adds `await prisma.credential.update(...)` at line 96 but never imports prisma, so `prisma` is a ReferenceError at runtime and the token refresh always crashes.

Stale credentials used for the jsforce Connection. After a successful refresh the code persists `accessTokenParsed.data` to the DB but then constructs the Connection from the old `credentialKey.instance_url / access_token / refresh_token` instead of `accessTokenParsed.data`. The refreshed access_token is never used, so the call immediately fails with the expired token.

achados.lines: if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: response.statusText });
achados.description: Incorrect HTTP error check. `fetch` Response.statusText is unreliable (often "" even on success, and not guaranteed to be "OK") — should check `!response.ok` or `response.status !== 200`. This either throws on successful 200 responses or misses real errors, and propagates an empty/incorrect message.

Bypasses the credential-sync abstraction. Every other OAuth CalendarService in this PR (google, office365, hubspot, lark, webex, etc.) wraps the fetch with `refreshOAuthTokens(..., appSlug, credential.userId)` to delegate to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true. Salesforce fetches directly, so credential sharing never works for Salesforce and breaks the contract introduced by the PR.

Returns raw fetch `Response` on the sync branch while `refreshFunction` returns caller-specific parsed types: Google expects `GaxiosResponse {data:{access_token}}` accessed as `res?.data`, HubSpot expects already-parsed `HubspotToken`. Sync branch returns `Response` which has no `.data` / token fields, so `token = res?.data` is undefined (Google CalendarService L94-96 TypeError on `token.access_token`) and `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn/accessToken` is undefined (Hubspot L191-192 -> NaN expiry, corrupt credential). One wrapper cannot satisfy both `Response`-expecting and object-expecting callers.

No HTTP error handling on sync fetch. `fetch` does not throw on 4xx/5xx, and code returns `response` without checking `response.ok` or calling `handleErrorsJson`/`handleErrorsRaw`. Callers that do `response.json()` or check `.data` will treat error pages as valid tokens, persisting garbage and masking refresh failures. Off-365 callers do `handleErrorsJson` on the returned value, but Google/HubSpot callers do not, so failure is silent.

No authentication forwarded to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. The `app-credential` webhook (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts L24-28) requires `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` header; the sync fetch sends only `calcomUserId`+`appSlug` as `URLSearchParams` with no secret header or signature. The endpoint cannot verify the caller is a legitimate Cal instance, and request body is not signed/encrypted.

Missing `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and incomplete payload. `new URLSearchParams` body sent without header may be rejected; more importantly only `userId`+`appSlug` sent, no `credentialId`/`teamId`. Team credentials have `userId==null` so `&& userId` (L5) is falsy and sync is silently skipped for team-owned calendars, falling back to local refresh even when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true, and endpoint cannot disambiguate multiple credentials for same user/app.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED the helper does `fetch(CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT)` and returns the raw fetch Response. GoogleCalendarService expects the refreshFunction to return a GaxiosResponse `{data:{access_token,expiry_date}}` (from `myGoogleAuth.refreshToken(...).res`) and does `const token = res?.data; token.access_token`. A fetch Response has no `.data`, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws TypeError — Google refresh is broken when sync is enabled. No `response.json()` or shape mapping is done.

Same contract break for Hubspot (and analogous for other apps). Hubspot does `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(()=> hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(...))` and then accesses `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn/accessToken/expiryDate`. Sync path returns a fetch Response instead of a HubspotToken object, so those fields are undefined, `expiryDate = Date.now()+expiresIn*1000` becomes NaN and credential update writes corrupt data.

No normalization or error handling: sync fetch is returned without checking `response.ok` and without parsing JSON. Callers are heterogeneous (Google expects `.data`, Office365/Lark/Webex expect fetch Response for `handleErrorsJson`/`handleLarkError`, Hubspot expects plain token object). Returning an unparsed Response leaks the abstraction, treats HTTP 4xx/5xx as success, and forces each caller to branch. Should parse `await response.json()` and map to the same shape `refreshFunction` returns, or throw on !ok.

Incorrect relative import: file is at `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts` but imports `decodeOAuthState` from `../oauth/decodeOAuthState`. That resolves to `.../_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState` via `../oauth/` indirection (up then back down) instead of `./decodeOAuthState`. It is a copy-paste error from moving both files into the `oauth/` subfolder (compare other moved files that correctly use `../../_utils/oauth/...`). Works by accident but is brittle, confusing, and will break with stricter resolvers/lint.

JSDoc is wrong/broken contract: both `@param appData.type` and `@param appData.appId` are documented as `the app slug`. In all callers `appId` is the slug (`google-calendar`, `hubspot`, `msteams`) and `type` is the credential type (`google_calendar`, `hubspot_other_calendar`, `office365_video`). Documenting both as slug misleads callers and hides the distinct meanings.

Privilege-escalation / dead admin check exposed by this region: region decodes `state.teamId` and claims to create team vs user credentials, but the team branch (lines 30-46) only checks `members.some {userId, accepted:true}` (any member) and `return`s early, while the `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` imported in this region (line 7) is called on line 59 with `state?.teamId ?? null` after the early return — so for team flow it never runs, and for user flow it is always `null` (no-op). Any team member (not admin) can create `teamId`-scoped credentials.

Privilege escalation / dead admin check: When state.teamId is present the code only verifies `members.some({userId, accepted:true})` (lines 32-43) and then `return`s (56). The intended admin check `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` on line 59 is therefore dead code — it is only reached when teamId is falsy (it receives `null` and early-returns). `getUserAdminTeams` requires `role in [ADMIN,OWNER]` but this path allows any accepted member to create a team-wide credential via `prisma.credential.create({teamId})`.

Unhandled exception from `decodeOAuthState(req)` : `decodeOAuthState` does `JSON.parse(req.query.state)` without try/catch or Zod validation (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9). A malformed or non-JSON `state` query param crashes `createOAuthAppCredential` with a 500 SyntaxError instead of a 400, and `teamId` is never validated to be a number (IntegrationOAuthCallbackState).

Wrong error contract: `throw new Error("User does not belong to the team")` should be `HttpError` (401/403). The generic Error bubbles as 500 Internal Server Error, inconsistent with the `HttpError(401)` used on line 25 and with `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` (401).

Brittle self-referential import: file is `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts` but imports `from "../oauth/decodeOAuthState"` which resolves to `oauth/oauth/decodeOAuthState` via `../oauth` (equivalent to `./decodeOAuthState`). Indicates the move from `_utils/` was not updated; works only by accident and will break with stricter resolvers.

Must be 32 bytes for AES256 but suggests `openssl rand -base64 24`. That generates 24 raw bytes (32 base64 chars). `packages/lib/crypto.ts:16,33` does `Buffer.from(key,'latin1')` so 32 chars -> 32 bytes but only 192-bit entropy, contradicting 256-bit claim. If user follows the intuitive `openssl rand -base64 32` (as on line 236, which yields 44 chars) the 44-byte latin1 key makes `crypto.createCipheriv/createDecipheriv` throw 'Invalid key length' at runtime in `symmetricEncrypt/symmetricDecrypt`.

Docs say header name should be in lowercase because `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25` does case-sensitive `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]` lookup (Next.js lowercases headers). Example includes quoted value "calcom-webhook-secret"; if env provider does not strip quotes, lookup is `"calcom-webhook-secret"` vs `calcom-webhook-secret` and all webhooks get 403. Comment does not warn that any uppercase or quoted value silently breaks authentication.

Block implies setting either secret enables sync, but `packages/lib/constants.ts:103-104` defines `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED = CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and `refreshOAuthTokens.ts`/`parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts` also require `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Setting only the webhook secret (per line 236) leaves feature disabled with 403 'Credential sharing is not enabled' with no documentation that both secrets (and endpoint for refresh) must be set together.

Wrong key-generation instruction for AES256. Comment says key "must be 32 bytes for AES256" but suggests `openssl rand -base64 24` (24 raw bytes, 32 base64 chars). `packages/lib/crypto.ts:15-19,32-37` does `Buffer.from(key,"latin1")` and `crypto.createCipheriv("aes256",...)` which requires exactly 32 bytes. A user following the sibling instruction `openssl rand -base64 32` (line 236) or who base64-decodes would get 44-char / 32-byte raw mismatch and `Invalid key length` at `symmetricDecrypt` in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:58`. Entropy and command are inconsistent and swapped.

Broken header-name contract. Docs say header name "Should be in lowercase" and example sets `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME="calcom-webhook-secret"`. `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25` does `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]` without `.toLowerCase()`. Node/Next lowercases incoming headers, so any non-lowercase env value silently fails lookup and rejects all valid webhooks with 403; code must normalize. Quoted default also risks literal quotes if env is injected without dotenv stripping.

Insecure/underspecified webhook auth. `.env.example` presents `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` as sole protection, but handler uses plain `!==` string equality (`app-credential.ts:25-26`) not `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, leaking timing, and does not restrict `req.method` (accepts GET/PUT) nor verify body signature. No guidance on secret strength/rotation; attacker can brute-force via timing oracle.

Undocumented interaction with sync endpoint weakens validation. Setting `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (empty in example) together with the two secrets enables `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (`packages/lib/constants.ts:103-104`). When enabled, `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15-16` downgrades strict `zod` schemas to `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (only `access_token` required) and `refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14` proxies refresh via unauthenticated `fetch` to arbitrary URL without sending `refresh_token`. Docs do not warn that strict token validation is disabled and that the external endpoint can inject arbitrary tokens persisted to `prisma.credential`.

JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")) is unguarded. symmetricDecrypt throws on bad key length / bad IV / wrong secret (and with fallback "" when env missing) and JSON.parse throws on non-JSON plaintext. Both throw as unhandled exceptions -> Next.js returns 500 and may leak stack, instead of 400. No Zod/schema validation of the decrypted payload either, so corrupted or attacker-controlled data crashes the handler.

findFirst({ where:{ userId, appId: appMetadata.slug }}) then separate update vs create is a classic TOCTOU race. No transaction, no unique constraint on (userId,appId) (schema.prisma Credential has no @@unique), and findFirst without order is nondeterministic if duplicates exist. Two concurrent webhook deliveries can both see no row and both create, leaving duplicate credentials for same user/app.

Decrypted keys are stored directly as credential.key (key: keys) with no validation and no re-encryption with CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Normal Cal.com credential handling encrypts sensitive fields at rest or validates against app-specific schemas (e.g., googleCredentialSchema). Here any JSON that decrypts correctly is persisted, allowing an attacker who obtains/ guesses the static webhook secret to overwrite any userId/appSlug credential with arbitrary JSON that will later be used as OAuth tokens.

symmetricDecrypt + JSON.parse are called with no try/catch. Invalid `keys`, wrong CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY length, or non-JSON plaintext throws from crypto.createDecipheriv / decipher.final / JSON.parse and bubbles as 500 with stack trace instead of 400. Breaks API contract and leaks internals.

Non-atomic findFirst then create/update race. Credential has no unique(userId,appId) constraint, so concurrent webhook calls can both miss and double-create duplicates. Comment claims cannot use upsert because id unknown, but upsert/transaction with unique where clause is required.

Decrypted keys are stored as plain Json object `key: keys`. CalDAV-derived apps (apple-calendar, exchange2013/2016, exchangecalendar - BaseCalendarService) expect `credential.key` to be a string `iv:ciphertext` encrypted with CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY and do `symmetricDecrypt(credential.key as string, CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)`. Webhook breaks that contract and will crash those services.

No schema validation of decrypted payload. Any JSON (string/number/null, missing access_token/refresh_token, extra fields) is persisted verbatim to credential.key. Later flows use zod schemas (googleCredentialSchema, salesforceTokenSchema, parseRefreshTokenResponse) and will fail, and allows an holder of the webhook secret to inject arbitrary credential content for any userId/appSlug.

Lookup is `where: { userId, appId: appMetadata.slug }` only. Ignores `type` discriminator (slug != type, e.g. google-calendar vs google_calendar) and teamId/userId distinction. For apps with multiple credential types or team credentials, findFirst can match/overwrite the wrong row or miss.

Uses `APP_NAME` for the From header (``${APP_NAME} <...>``) instead of `EMAIL_FROM_NAME` like every other Organizer email (`OrganizerScheduledEmail`, `OrganizerRequestEmail`). This ignores the `EMAIL_FROM_NAME` env override (`process.env.EMAIL_FROM_NAME || APP_NAME`) and violates the established contract for sender name.

Unsafe `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` without guard/fallback. If `attendees` is empty it throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`. Even when non-empty, newly added guests are created with `name: ""` in `addGuests.handler.ts`, so if the first element is a guest the interpolated `{{name}}` in `guests_added_event_type_subject` becomes empty, producing a broken subject like `Guests Added: X with  at ...`.

Handles `teamMember` for `to` (`toAddresses`) but does not forward `teamMember` to `renderEmail` and does not use `teamMember.language` for `this.t`/subject. Base `OrganizerScheduledEmail` passes `teamMember` to the React template and uses it for locale/timeZone. Here a round-robin team member receives organizer-personalized HTML/subject in the wrong locale/timezone.

Uses `APP_NAME` for the `from` header (`from: `${APP_NAME} <...>`) instead of `EMAIL_FROM_NAME`. Every other organizer template (organizer-scheduled-email.ts:6,47, organizer-location-change-email.ts:1,23, etc.) uses `EMAIL_FROM_NAME = process.env.EMAIL_FROM_NAME || APP_NAME` so custom `EMAIL_FROM_NAME` env is respected. This wrapper breaks that contract and makes the sender name unconfigurable/hardcoded to "Cal.com".

Unsafe `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` for subject interpolation. If `attendees` is empty it throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')` and crashes sendAddGuestsEmails. Even when non-empty, `addGuests.handler.ts:84` creates new guests with `name: ""`, so if `attendees[0]` resolves to a newly-added guest the subject becomes `Guests Added: {{eventType}} with  at {{date}}` (empty name). AttendeeAddGuestsEmail correctly falls back to `team?.name || organizer.name`; organizer version needs `attendees[0]?.name || attendees[0]?.email || organizer.name` guard.

isInvalidEmail is set to true on validation failure but never cleared: not reset on input change (setValue), not reset when validation succeeds, and not reset in addGuestsMutation onSuccess (which resets multiEmailValue but not the error flag). Once shown the 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error persists across retries and even after a successful add, and will be stale on next dialog open.

Stale dialog state leak: multiEmailValue is initialized to [""] and only reset on Cancel and onSuccess. Dialog onOpenChange is wired directly to setIsOpenDialog, so closing via overlay/Escape does not reset multiEmailValue or isInvalidEmail. Reopening shows previous emails/error. Conversely MultiEmail allows deleting the last field to get [] which makes handleAdd hit `if (length===0) return` with no feedback, while the initial [""] defeats that guard and always triggers validation failure.

Broken error toast fallback: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`` is always truthy (e.g. "undefined: ..." when code missing), so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never falls back. User sees "undefined: <message>" instead of localized "unable_to_add_guests" when err.data.code is undefined.

Divergent / client-only validation: ZAddGuestsInputSchema is re-defined inside the component with .refine(unique) but the server schema in addGuests.schema.ts is just z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness check. Duplicates like ["a@a.com","a@a.com"] are blocked only client-side and can be sent via direct tRPC call; server handler's uniqueGuests filter only dedupes against existing attendees, so createMany would create duplicate attendee rows.

Case-sensitive uniqueness and email check: refine uses `new Set(emails)` and z.string().email() without normalization/trim/lowercasing, so "Test@example.com" vs "test@example.com" passes as unique and " a@b.com " fails inconsistently. Server also compares case-sensitively and blacklist check lowercases only the list, allowing bypass.

multiEmailValue initialized to [""] so length is 1, making `if (multiEmailValue.length===0) return` dead for the initial empty field. Validation then fails via zod ("" is not an email) and shows generic uniqueness error. Conversely after user removes the last field via MultiEmail X, value becomes [] and handleAdd silently returns with no toast/error, leaving user with no feedback. Empty-string vs empty-array states are conflated.

isInvalidEmail is set to true on validation failure but never cleared when multiEmailValue changes or when validation later succeeds. The error banner "emails_must_be_unique_valid" sticks forever after one failure until Cancel is clicked, even if user corrects the emails.

Client schema does .refine uniqueness check, server ZAddGuestsInputSchema is just z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness. Handler's uniqueGuests filter only removes emails already in booking.attendees, not duplicates within the request itself. Bypassing client (or race) sends ["a@b.com","a@b.com"] -> handler createMany inserts two Attendee rows with same email, duplicate DB records.

Dialog sends raw multiEmailValue without trim()/toLowerCase(). Handler lowercases blacklist but checks !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) with guest not lowercased, and compares booking.attendees with strict ===. So "Test@Example.com" vs "test@example.com" is considered unique and BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS can be bypassed by case (e.g., SPAM@blocked.com), leading to duplicate attendees and blacklist bypass.

Dialog onOpenChange is set directly to setIsOpenDialog. Closing via overlay/Esc calls setIsOpenDialog(false) without resetting multiEmailValue or isInvalidEmail (unlike Cancel/Success handlers). Next open reuses stale emails and stale isInvalidEmail error, leaking state across opens.

Handler computes isTeamAdminOrOwner as (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)). Requires user to be BOTH admin AND owner simultaneously, which is impossible. Legitimate team admins/owners calling the dialog's trpc.viewer.bookings.addGuests will get FORBIDDEN incorrectly; should be ||.

casa.which: 7 (defect 1 is identical duplicate — both 1 and 7 describe the same cause: isInvalidEmail set true on validation failure never cleared on multiEmailValue/input change or on validation-success/success path, and same consequence: 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' banner persists forever even after fixing emails/retries)

achados.description: Server schema guests: z.array(z.string().email()) does not enforce uniqueness, but client does (AddGuestsDialog refine with Set). Direct tRPC call can send duplicates e.g. ["a@b.com","a@b.com"]. Handler's uniqueGuests only filters against existing attendees/blacklist, not duplicates within request, so createMany will insert duplicate Attendee rows with same email and send duplicate emails.

Schema allows empty array guests: [] . Client guards length===0, but server permits it; handler then throws BAD_REQUEST with misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' after filtering. Should be .nonempty() / .min(1) to reject at validation layer with correct error.

No upper bound on guests array (.max()). Attacker can bypass UI and send thousands of emails in one request causing unbounded prisma createMany rows, EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees and sendAddGuestsEmails fan-out, enabling DoS/spam. Client has no limit either.

No normalization (.trim()/.toLowerCase()/.transform). Emails are case-sensitive for uniqueness and blacklist checks. Handler lowercases BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS but compares with raw guest string (!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)) and uses guest === attendee.email, so 'User@Example.com' vs 'user@example.com' bypasses duplicate and blacklist detection.

bookingId uses z.number() with no int/positive/finite check. Accepts NaN, Infinity, floats and negative ids. Other booking inputs use commonBookingSchema but same looseness; here it is exposed as public tRPC input so Prisma is hit with invalid ids (prisma.booking.findFirst where id: NaN/ -1 / 1.5) wasting DB roundtrip and leaking confusing NOT_FOUND vs validation errors. Should be z.number().int().positive().

guests: z.array(z.string().email()) lacks .nonempty()/.min(1). Empty array passes Zod and reaches handler, which then filters to uniqueGuests=[] and throws TRPCError BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' — misleading message and unnecessary DB fetch (booking + organizer lookup). Client guards with length===0 but server must be source of truth; schema should reject [] with proper Zod error.

No uniqueness refinement and no max length, unlike client AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29 which does .refine(unique). Server therefore accepts duplicate emails and unbounded arrays. Handler's deduplication only checks against existing DB attendees (guest===attendee.email) not intra-array duplicates and is case-sensitive, so ['a@x.com','a@x.com'] or ['A@x.com','a@x.com'] both pass and createMany inserts duplicate Attendee rows (or violates unique constraint), and eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees + sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) are called with original guests including blacklisted/existing duplicates, causing wrong email branching and enabling DoS/spam by sending thousands of guests to create thousands of rows and Promise.all email sends.

Blacklist/duplicate filter is case-sensitive while blacklist is lowercased: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is `toLowerCase()` but `guest` and `attendee.email` are compared with `===`/`includes` without lowercasing. `Guest@blocked.com` bypasses `guest@blocked.com` blacklist and `User@Example.com` vs `user@example.com` bypasses existing-attendee check, so filtered `uniqueGuests` is incorrect and `prisma.booking.update` createMany at 98-106 persists blacklisted/duplicate attendees.

Intra-request duplicates not handled. Backend `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (addGuests.schema.ts) is `z.array(z.string().email())` without uniqueness refine (frontend has refine), and `uniqueGuests` at 74-78 only filters against existing attendees/blacklist, not against duplicates within `guests` itself. `guests=["a@b.com","a@b.com"]` passes through, `guestsFullDetails` contains duplicate emails, and `createMany` at 98-106 tries to create duplicate `Attendee` rows for same booking -> duplicates or Prisma unique-constraint P2002 500.

`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` at 168 is called with original `guests` instead of filtered/normalized `uniqueGuests`. `email-manager.ts:541` does `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` case-sensitive to decide `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (new) vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (existing). Passing unfiltered `guests` misclassifies: existing attendees that were filtered out still match as new, and case-variant duplicates mismatch. Also `evt.attendees` built in region 108-136 already contains the newly created attendees, amplifying the mismatch. Should pass `uniqueGuests` lowercased/normalized.

Authorization is `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` instead of `||`. `isTeamAdmin` already returns truthy for ADMIN or OWNER, so `&& isTeamOwner` collapses to OWNER-only. A team ADMIN (non-OWNER) is incorrectly FORBIDDEN from lines 92-106, while the intended policy was ADMIN OR OWNER OR organizer OR attendee.

Deduplication/blacklist is case-sensitive and whitespace-sensitive: `guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compare raw strings while blacklist is lowercased. `Aa@x.com` vs `aa@x.com` bypasses dedup and blacklist, and duplicates *within* the input `guests` array are not de-duplicated at all (schema does not enforce uniqueness). `createMany` at 100-105 then creates duplicate Attendee rows differing only by case/whitespace or two identical rows in one request.

Backend stores `uniqueGuests` filtered list but `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` at 168 sends the original unfiltered `guests`. Combined with case-sensitive `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in email-manager, newly added guests whose casing differs get misclassified (existing attendees get Scheduled template, new guests get AddGuests template) and blacklisted/duplicate addresses that were filtered from the DB still affect email routing. Should use the normalized `uniqueGuests`.

Calendar sync uses requester's credentials `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` at 158. When an attendee (allowed by 52) or team admin adds guests, the EventManager is constructed with the requester's calendars, not the organizer's (`booking.userId`). `updateCalendarAttendees` (which no-ops if `booking.references.length===0`) will not update the organizer's destination calendar, leaving external calendar out-of-sync. Moreover DB `booking.update` at 92-106 is committed before calendar update with no transaction/rollback — partial failure leaves DB attendees added but calendar unchanged, and error is not handled.

Initial state `useState([""])` embeds an invalid empty email. This makes `handleAdd`'s `if (multiEmailValue.length===0) return` dead (length is 1) and forces `MultiEmail` to render an empty input that always fails `z.string().email()` validation. Correct empty state is `[]` (which `MultiEmail` already handles via the "Add Emails" button). If validation were skipped, it would send `[""]` to the server.

`isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on validation failure but never cleared: `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` only runs in Cancel handler (88-93) and not on `onChange`/`setMultiEmailValue`, not on successful validation, not in `onSuccess` (36-41), and not when `Dialog onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` closes via overlay/Esc. Error therefore sticks after user corrects input and persists across re-opens.

Client validation `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(arr=>new Set(arr).size===arr.length)` is case- and whitespace-sensitive (no `.trim()`/`.toLowerCase()`). `Test@ex.com` vs `test@ex.com` or `" test@ex.com "` bypass uniqueness. Server's `addGuests.handler.ts:70-77` lowercases `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` but compares `!blacklisted.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`, and checks `guest===attendee.email` case-sensitive, so blacklist/duplicate checks can be bypassed via case variation that client incorrectly considers unique/valid.

`Dialog open={isOpenDialog} onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` delegates close to the parent setter without resetting `multiEmailValue`/`isInvalidEmail`. Closing via outside click or Esc (which triggers `onOpenChange(false)`) leaves stale emails and stale `isInvalidEmail` state for the next open; only Cancel and `onSuccess` reset the value, and `onSuccess` doesn't reset `isInvalidEmail`. Needs `useEffect` on `isOpenDialog` or a wrapped `onOpenChange` to clear state.

Client Zod schema uses `new Set(emails)` for uniqueness without normalizing. `a@b.com` and `A@B.COM` / ` a@b.com ` are considered distinct, but emails are case-insensitive. Bypasses uniqueness and mismatches server duplicate/blacklist logic which should be case-insensitive.

Client enforces uniqueness via `.refine(unique)` but server `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts:3-6` is `z.array(z.string().email())` with no refine. Direct tRPC call bypasses client check and creates duplicate `attendee` rows in `prisma.booking.update createMany`.

`isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on validation failure but never reset on subsequent `setMultiEmailValue` changes or on successful validation/mutation. Error banner `emails_must_be_unique_valid` stays visible after user fixes input; only Cancel clears it.

Initial state `[""]` and `handleAdd` `if (multiEmailValue.length===0) return` are inconsistent. Deleting all fields yields `[]` which silently does nothing with no feedback, while `[""]` triggers validation error. Empty strings are not filtered/trimmed before `safeParse`/`mutate`, so `mutate({guests:[""]})` would be blocked client-side but `multiEmailValue` containing `"", " "` is treated as real input.

Guests are sent raw (`multiEmailValue`) without `trim()`/`toLowerCase()`. Server `addGuests.handler.ts:70-77` lowercases `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` but compares `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` and `guest===attendee.email` case-sensitively, so `User@Blacklisted.com` or ` test@example.com ` bypasses blacklist and duplicate filtering introduced by the dialog.

Passes `onClickAddon`/`addOnSuffix` to `EmailField` imported from `@calcom/ui`. That re-export comes from `packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx` (and `form/fields.tsx`) whose `InputField`/`EmailField` does NOT implement `addOnSuffix`/`onClickAddon` – only `packages/ui/components/form/inputs/TextField.tsx:66` does. The props are spread as unknown attributes to the native `<input>` and no `Addon` wrapper is rendered, so the ‘x’ remove suffix never appears and guests cannot be removed.

Even if the add-on capable `InputField` were used, the visible `<button type="button">` inside `addOnSuffix` has no `onClick`; the handler is on the parent `Addon` div via `onClickAddon` (`TextField.tsx:39`). The div is not focusable/keyboard operable, has no role/aria-label, and `Tooltip` portals/ stops propagation, so keyboard/a11y removal is broken and clicks are brittle (rely on bubbling from button to div). Handler should be on the button with an accessible name.

List items use `key={index}` for a dynamic list mutated with `splice`/`push` (lines 41,66,85). When an email in the middle is removed, React reuses DOM nodes for the wrong index, causing stale `value={field}` display, focus loss, and deleting/editing the wrong row. Use stable key (e.g., derived from value+index or id).

Self-import `from "@calcom/ui"` inside `packages/ui` (MultiEmail is part of that package, re-exported via `MultiEmailLazy.tsx`) creates a circular dependency. At build/runtime the imported `EmailField`/`Button`/`Tooltip` can be undefined or stale and breaks tree-shaking. Use relative imports e.g. `../components/form/...`.

Uses index as key (`key={index}`) for dynamic email list. When an email is removed via `onClickAddon` splice, React reuses DOM nodes by index, so the input that stays mounted shows the wrong value / cursor jumps. Deleting the middle guest can appear to delete the last one and sends the wrong email array to AddGuestsDialog / server.

Remove control is broken by nesting: `addOnSuffix` renders `<Tooltip><button type="button">` inside InputField's `Addon` `<div onClick={onClickAddon}>`. The `button` has no `onClick`; reliance on bubbling to the parent `div` is fragile (Tooltip portals/stops propagation, invalid nested interactive content, keyboard activation on button does not trigger div handler). User may be unable to remove an email, leaving empty/invalid entries stuck in `value`.

onChange stores raw `e.target.value` without `trim()` or `toLowerCase()`. AddGuestsDialog's `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` uniqueness `new Set(emails).size===length` and the server's `uniqueGuests` filter (`guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`) are all case/whitespace sensitive. `A@b.com` vs `a@b.com` or `a@b.com ` bypasses duplicate and blacklist (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` is lowercased) checks, allowing duplicate attendee rows and blacklist bypass.

No inline validation or error reset: `required` on `EmailField` is inert outside a native `<form>` and the component never clears parent `isInvalidEmail`. After `handleAdd` sets `isInvalidEmail=true`, subsequent edits via `setValue` do not reset it, so the error banner persists indefinitely. Combined with allowing `value=["",""]` to be built via Add button, user gets only a generic submit-time error.

Permission check uses `&&` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner: `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner`. Since isTeamAdmin already returns truthy for ADMIN||OWNER, the AND requires OWNER, so pure ADMINs are denied. This contradicts intent of `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and blocks legitimate team admins. Should be `||` (and handle isTeamAdmin returning object vs boolean).

Duplicate/blacklist filtering is case-sensitive: `guest === attendee.email` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lower-casing `guest`. Blacklist entries are lower-cased but guest is not, so `Test@Example.com` bypasses duplicate check and blacklist via case variation, creating duplicate Attendee rows and bypassing blocklist.

Emails are sent with original `guests` array instead of filtered `uniqueGuests`. `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` causes newGuests.includes check to mis-classify already-existing or blacklisted emails as new, sending AttendeeScheduledEmail to wrong recipients and leaking invite vs update semantics. Should pass `uniqueGuests`.

Calendar update uses `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (the caller) instead of organizer's credentials. When an attendee (allowed by line 52) adds guests, the EventManager is constructed with the attendee's credentials, so calendar attendees won't be updated on the organizer's calendar. Also DB attendees are created before calendar update with no transaction/rollback - if updateCalendarAttendees throws, DB is left inconsistent.

Dialog initializes `multiEmailValue` to `[""]` (single empty string) which always fails `z.string().email()` validation, and `isInvalidEmail` is set true on failure but never cleared on input change or on successful validation/mutation. Error banner persists even after fixing emails, and clearing all inputs to `[]` hits early return `if(length===0) return` with no user feedback, while empty array would otherwise pass server schema.

Authorization check uses `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` instead of `||`. `isTeamAdmin` already returns truthy for ADMIN or OWNER, `isTeamOwner` only for OWNER, so `&&` requires OWNER. Team ADMINs (non-owners) are incorrectly denied. Should be `||` (or just `isTeamAdmin`). Existing team handlers use `||`.

Dedup/blacklist is case-sensitive and incomplete: `guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compare raw strings, but `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lower-cased. An attacker can bypass blacklist with `User@Example.COM` and can create duplicate attendees with different casing or whitespace. Filter also doesn't deduplicate within `guests` itself, only against existing attendees.

Calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original unfiltered `guests` array instead of `uniqueGuests` (filtered for existing/blacklisted). Blacklisted/duplicate/empty entries are then treated as `newGuests` in `email-manager.ts:541` `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (case-sensitive), sending wrong template (`AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`) and leaking intent to add blacklisted addresses.

Server Zod schema is `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness/refine, while client validates uniqueness. Backend therefore accepts `guests: ["a@b.com","a@b.com"]`. Handler's `uniqueGuests` only filters against existing attendees, not within the array, so `createMany` creates duplicate Attendee rows.

Permission check includes `isAttendee` as sufficient (`booking.attendees.find(email===user.email)`). Any attendee can call `addGuests` to inject arbitrary additional guests into a booking, escalating privileges. Intended policy is organizer / team admin/owner only.

Add Guests action is pushed to `editBookingActions` unconditionally, with no guard for cancelled/rejected/past bookings or seated events. `bookedActions` only filters `edit_booking` for recurring tabs, so user can open `AddGuestsDialog` for a `CANCELLED` or past booking and the handler has no status check, creating attendees and calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` on an invalid booking.

Plural branch calls `obj[k].map(...)` without verifying `obj[k]` is an Array. If server sends null/undefined/non-array for `*_ids` (empty relation, missing key coerced to null), this throws TypeError and breaks hydration, whereas singular branch safely handles missing values via `_lookupSubType` returning falsy.

Plural hydration does not filter failed lookups: `map(id => _lookupSubType(...))` returns `undefined` when id not found in `root` (missing collection or unknown id). Result array contains `undefined` entries (e.g., `[undefined, model]`) instead of compacted models. `hydrated || []` is dead code because `map` always returns a truthy Array, so empty/missing case never falls back and undefined entries leak to consumers (`colors.length` counts undefineds, `get('id')` crashes).

Inconsistent `delete` semantics: singular `*_id` only deletes the foreign-key property when hydration succeeds (`if (hydrated) { obj[subType]=hydrated; delete obj[k]; }`), preserving the original key for debugging/fallback. Plural `*_ids` unconditionally does `obj[plural]=hydrated; delete obj[k];` even when all lookups failed, deleting source ids and replacing them with an array of undefineds — data loss and broken contract compared to singular path.

Plural branch does obj[k].map(...) unconditionally. If the payload has *_ids == null, undefined, or not an array (nullable field, empty, or single value) this throws TypeError and crashes _hydrate/_hydrateEmbedded. Singular branch handled missing/falsy gracefully via falsy hydrated check.

Plural branch always does obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || [] and delete obj[k] even when lookups fail. hydrated is always an Array from .map so || [] is dead code. Failed lookups become undefined entries in the array ([undefined, undefined]) and original *_ids is lost. Singular branch only deletes when hydrated truthy, preserving the id for fallback/debugging. Inconsistent contract and data-loss.

Does not compact failed lookups. Array will contain undefined/null for any id not found in root or for embeddable-host/category miss, so consumers like fruit.get('colors')[i].get('id') throw and length is wrong. Should filter falsy results.

Uses naive self.pluralize(subType) (adds 's') for both collection lookup and property name. Irregular plurals break: e.g. category_ids => subType=category => pluralize => 'categorys' instead of 'categories' (used by serializers/root key and expected by callers). Lookup root['categorys'] misses and assignment creates wrong property, so data never hydrates.

before_validation does `self.host.sub!` without guarding for nil/blank. If `host` is nil (e.g. missing param `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` or direct `EmbeddableHost.new(host: nil)`), it raises `NoMethodError: undefined method `sub!' for nil` instead of failing validation. Should be `self.host = self.host.to_s.strip` guard or `if self.host.present?`.

Case-insensitive lookup is broken: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` does not downcase the input `host`. `URI#host` preserves case, so `http://EVILTROUT.COM` or mixed-case stored values will not match despite intent to be case-insensitive. Should be `host.downcase` (or `lower(?)`) and stored hosts should be normalized to downcase on save.

Port handling is inconsistent: `before_validation` keeps `:port` (validation regex allows `:[0-9]{1,5}` and only strips protocol and `/path`), so `https://example.com:3000/foo` is stored as `example.com:3000`. But `record_for_host` uses `URI(host).host` which discards the port, then queries `lower(host)=?` with just `example.com`. Hosts configured with a port will never match, and hosts without a port will incorrectly allow any port.

Contract confusion: `record_for_host` returns `false` on parse failure instead of `nil`. Callers expect nil/falsy record (e.g. `TopicEmbed` does `eh = record_for_host(url); eh.try(:category_id)` and `host_allowed?` uses `.present?`). Returning `false` is non-idiomatic for a finder, hides intent, and `false.try(:category_id)` returns nil via ActiveSupport but obscures error handling; should return `nil`.

before_validation assumes self.host is a String. If host is nil (e.g., params missing or blank) self.host.sub! raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error. Controller Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host assigns params directly and falls back to uncategorized only for category_id, so a nil host crashes on save.

before_validation strips scheme with /^https?:\/\// (case-sensitive). An uppercase input like 'HTTP://example.com' is not stripped, so it is stored with scheme, fails to normalize and will never match host_allowed? which extracts uri.host (without scheme). Should be /i.

record_for_host extracts uri.host which excludes port, but validations and before_validation allow/store 'host:port' (e.g. 'example.com:8080'). Query where("lower(host) = ?", host) compares bare hostname to 'host:port' and never matches. Also host param is not downcased, so WHERE lower(host)=? with mixed-case 'EVILTROUT.COM' misses stored 'eviltrout.com'.

record_for_host requires a URI with scheme: URI('eviltrout.com').host is nil, so it returns false for bare hostnames. Callers pass referer/embed_url with scheme today, but any direct host check or future caller fails. Also returns `false` instead of `nil` on not-found/invalid URI, breaking ActiveRecord convention and forcing callers to rely on .present?; e.g. TopicEmbed sets eh = record_for_host(url); eh.try(:category_id) works by accident but type is wrong.

Only validates_format_of :host, no validates_presence or validates_uniqueness (case-insensitive). Blank string bypasses before_validation and format handles it, but nil crashes; duplicates with different case or with/without port/scheme can be created, leaving ambiguous host_allowed? and category selection. Migration also inserts raw site_settings values without normalizing/stripping or escaping, so migrated rows retain 'http://' and paths while new rows are stripped, creating inconsistent matching.

Test named 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' is vacuous/false-positive and mismatches new implementation. It sets no preconditions (no `embed_truncate=true`, no `has_topic_embed?=true`) so `expandable_first_post?` returns false because `has_topic_embed?` is false (Topic built unsaved) and `embed_truncate` defaults false, not because host is blank. New `Topic#expandable_first_post?` (app/models/topic.rb:868-869) is `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` with no host check, so with `embed_truncate=true` and `has_topic_embed?=true` it would return true even when no EmbeddableHost exists, contradicting the test's name/claim. Test therefore documents and appears to verify a contract that code no longer enforces.

Coverage loss / broken contract after removing `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` check: PR deletes the host-presence guard in `Topic#expandable_first_post?` instead of replacing with `EmbeddableHost.exists?`/`EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`. Spec moves the true-case into `describe 'with an emeddable host' [sic] with `before { Fabricate(:embeddable_host); SiteSetting.embed_truncate=true; stub has_topic_embed? }` but never tests the complementary blank-host + same preconditions case. So regression (topics with embeds remain expandable after all hosts deleted, or truncated embeds shown when embedding not configured) is not caught, and inner tests inherit host-dependent setup without isolating host vs truncate vs embed factors.

Test titled "is false if embeddable_host is blank" does not check what it claims. Old implementation was `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` and test set `embed_truncate=true` + `has_topic_embed?=true` then nulled hosts to isolate host variable. New `Topic#expandable_first_post?` at app/models/topic.rb:868-870 is just `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` with no host check, and new test never sets `embed_truncate=true` nor stubs `has_topic_embed?=true`. It passes vacuously (defaults are false/nil) even if a host exists, and hides that expansion is now allowed with zero `EmbeddableHost` rows. It is wrong documentation and a false-positive / broken contract.

Context `describe 'with an emeddable host'` (typo) fabricates an `EmbeddableHost` in a before block but `expandable_first_post?` no longer reads `EmbeddableHost` at all. The fabrication is dead code; the three inner examples would have identical results without it, so the test misleads that a host is a precondition for `true` and for the `embed_truncate?`/`has_topic_embed?` false-cases. Coverage is misleading: no example verifies that `expandable_first_post?` is true/false independent of host presence, which is the actual post-PR behavior.

Test titled 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' is vacuous/broken contract. It does not set SiteSetting.embed_truncate=true nor stub has_topic_embed?=true, so Topic#expandable_first_post? (app/models/topic.rb:869) returns false due to those defaults (has_topic_embed? false via DB query on unpersisted topic, embed_truncate false) not due to blank hosts. After PR the method no longer checks SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts nor EmbeddableHost at all (changed to `embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`), yet this example still claims to cover the blank-host case and will stay green regardless. It therefore does not check what it claims and hides that the host-gating contract was dropped vs migrated to EmbeddableHost.exists?.

describe 'with an emeddable host' / before { Fabricate(:embeddable_host) } is dead/misleading setup. Topic#expandable_first_post? ignores EmbeddableHost (app/models/topic.rb:868-869), so the fabricated host is never read and the 'is true with correct settings and topic_embed' example passes even with zero hosts. The describe implies host presence is a precondition, contradicting the implementation. Either the model is missing a host check (should be EmbeddableHost.exists?/any? if gating was intended) or the spec is wrong documentation that wastes DB state and gives false confidence about embedding gating.

Test titled 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' does not test host blank. It leaves SiteSetting.embed_truncate at default false and does not stub has_topic_embed? (returns false via DB query on unpersisted Fabricate.build(:topic)). So expandable_first_post? returns false for unrelated reasons (truncate false / no embed). It would still pass if implementation returned true when truncate true + has_topic_embed true + no host, so it does not verify the claimed host condition and gives false confidence. With new Topic#expandable_first_post? (SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?) host is no longer checked, making the title stale/wrong documentation.

Context 'with an emeddable host' Fabricates an EmbeddableHost but Topic#expandable_first_post? no longer reads EmbeddableHost (PR removed SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts check without replacing with EmbeddableHost.exists?). The setup is dead/misleading. If contract should still require at least one host, implementation is buggy (missing host check) and tests do not catch it. If host check intentionally removed, the fabrication and description are stale and the complementary case (truncate true + has_topic_embed true + NO host => true) is never exercised.

Missing/incorrect coverage for new contract. No test sets SiteSetting.embed_truncate=true and has_topic_embed?=true with zero hosts to explicitly assert behavior. Combined with shared let(:topic){Fabricate.build(:topic)} (unsaved, id nil, so real has_topic_embed? always false without stub), the suite cannot distinguish 'false because no host' vs 'false because truncate false / no embed', leaving regression undetected. Also typo 'emeddable' indicates stale docs.

Null dereference: document.getElementById('discourse-comments') can return null if element absent or script runs before DOM ready (IIFE executes immediately, no DOMContentLoaded check). Unconditional comments.appendChild(iframe) then throws TypeError and aborts embedding. No null guard or deferred execution.

Insecure/broken postMessage origin check: discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 checks if e.origin is substring of discourseUrl instead of strict origin equality. Should parse discourseUrl to origin (scheme+host+port) and compare e.origin === expectedOrigin. Substring check is bypassable (e.g., e.origin='http://exam' is substring of 'http://example.com/') and brittle to trailing slash/path/port. Also throws if discourseUrl undefined.

URL construction assumes trailing slash: discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + ... produces malformed URL when discourseUrl lacks trailing slash (e.g., 'https://forum.example.com' => 'https://forum.example.comembed/best?...' -> 404). No normalization of slash between base and path.

Unchecked globals discourseUrl / discourseEmbedUrl: declared only as /* global */ for linter, no runtime typeof check. If not defined, line 7 encodeURIComponent(discourseEmbedUrl) yields "undefined" and line 17 discourseUrl.indexOf throws ReferenceError/TypeError, breaking embed. Should guard with typeof discourseUrl === 'string' etc.

Unvalidated resize height: e.data.height is used as iframe.height = e.data.height + "px" without numeric validation/clamping and via height attribute not style.height. Malicious or buggy sender (especially with weak origin check) can set arbitrary/NaN/very large height causing layout breakage/DoS. Should verify Number.isFinite, clamp range, and set iframe.style.height.

document.getElementById('discourse-comments') can return null (element missing or script runs before DOM is ready - IIFE executes immediately with no DOMContentLoaded guard). Calling comments.appendChild(iframe) then throws TypeError and breaks embedding. No null check.

discourseUrl and discourseEmbedUrl are bare globals. If the host page forgets to define them, accessing them throws ReferenceError (not just undefined) because typeof check is missing. The /* global */ comment only silences linter. Line 7 and line 17 will crash.

iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..." assumes discourseUrl ends with trailing slash. If set as "https://discourse.example.com" (common), result is "https://discourse.example.comembed/best..." 404 / broken contract with GET embed/best route. No slash handling or URL parsing.

Origin validation is reversed and insecure: discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 checks if origin is substring of discourseUrl instead of e.origin === expectedOrigin. This is overly permissive (any substring of discourseUrl like "https://" as prefix would pass if attacker could set origin to that, and legitimate origin comparison should parse origin via URL) and fragile (discourseUrl includes path, so direct string containment is wrong). Correct is strict equality against new URL(discourseUrl).origin. Also allows arbitrary height resize if bypassed.

Stored XSS via raw_html bypass: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` skips PrettyText.cook / html-sanitizer-bundle, `add_rel_nofollow`, and any sanitization. `TopicEmbed.import` (used by `PollFeed` via `i.content.scrub` and by `import_remote` via Readability) and the appended `<a href='#{url}'>` store arbitrary external HTML as `raw`, then `PostCreator.before_create_tasks` saves `post.cooked = post.cook(raw)` => raw unsanitized. Embed view `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` does `<%= raw post.cooked %>` and normal views also render `cooked` unescaped. Attacker-controlled feed can inject <script>, <iframe>, on* handlers, etc. that execute in viewers' browsers.

Bypasses Plugin::Filter and cooking pipeline contract: regular path is `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, self, post_analyzer.cook(*args))` but raw_html path returns `raw` directly without filter. Plugins expecting `after_post_cook` to normalize/sanitize/linkify cooked HTML are silently skipped for imported posts, breaking expected invariant and allowing alternative XSS vectors to remain unfiltered.

XSS via complete sanitizer bypass: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` skips PrettyText.markdown/html-sanitizer-bundle (whitelist/nofollow/script stripping). TopicEmbed.import (RSS via PollFeed and remote via Readability) and PollFeed store arbitrary external HTML (`i.content`, `doc.content`) as `raw` with `cook_method=:raw_html` and `skip_validations:true`. `before_create` does `post.cooked ||= post.cook(...)` so cooked==raw unsanitized, later rendered in `embed/best.html.erb` via `raw post.cooked` and in topic views. RSS path has no HTML whitelist at all; even Readability path limited tags allow ``/`` and rss footer interpolates `url` unsanitized.

Unsanitized URL interpolation + no scheme filtering: TopicEmbed.import appends `link: "#{url}"` with external `url` (i.link/i.id or embed_url) without escaping/validating. Combined with raw_html bypass and TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls only handling leading '/' (`href.start_with?('/')`), dangerous schemes `javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:` and attribute breakouts via `'`/`"` in URL are preserved verbatim in cooked and executed on render.

Untrusted mass-assignment of cook_method: `PostCreator#setup_post` does `post.cook_method=@opts[:cook_method] if present?` with no authorization/trust check. Any controller/API that passes user-controlled opts can set `cook_method=Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (2) to bypass markdown/sanitizer for an arbitrary post. Enum default is 1 (:regular) but column is integer with no validation that only staff/embed flow may use 2, so bypass is exposed beyond the intended embed/RSS flow. Also skips `Plugin::Filter.after_post_cook` and `add_rel_nofollow_to_user_content`.

feed_key is defined but never referenced. Intended for conditional GET / ETag / If-Modified-Since caching to avoid re-fetching unchanged feeds, but poll_feed unconditionally does open+parse every hour. Dead code indicates incomplete optimization and wasted bandwidth/DB work (import still re-checks SHA but after full download).

open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) has no rescue/timeout/validation. Network errors (HTTPError, SocketError, Timeout), invalid XML, or SSRF values (file://, pipe '|') will raise and bubble out of a Jobs::Scheduled with retry:false, aborting the whole run. In TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve this aborts the fallback fetch_http path. Also bare Kernel#open with open-uri can interpret leading '|' as pipe command and file:// disclosure; no URI.scheme check and file descriptor is leaked (open without block).

Return value of SimpleRSS.parse is not checked. On empty/invalid/non-RSS body it returns nil/false, so rss.items raises NoMethodError and kills the job. Same if feed has no items (rss.items nil). No handling for feed fetch returning nil or rss.items being empty.

content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) assumes i.content is a non-nil String. Many RSS/Atom feeds put body in description or content:encoded, so i.content is nil -> NoMethodError on nil.scrub. Also String#scrub exists only Ruby >=2.1, will raise on 1.9/2.0 which Discourse 2013 target supported. No fallback to i.description and no nil guard before TopicEmbed.import.

Content/URL handling is insecure and incomplete: fallback url = i.id may still be non-http (urn:uuid, tag: URI) so TopicEmbed.import silently drops it; more importantly feed HTML is taken verbatim (only unescapeHTML) and stored with cook_method :raw_html (Post#cook bypasses pipeline) and rendered via raw in embed, so unsanitized script/onclick in feed becomes stored XSS. URL is later interpolated in TopicEmbed.import as "<a href='#{url}'>" without escaping single-quote, allowing attribute injection.

Missing `require 'cgi'` and nil handling for RSS fields: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` raises `NameError` (CGI not required) and `NoMethodError` when `i.content` is nil. Standard RSS/Atom uses `description` or `content:encoded`, not `content`; SimpleRSS therefore yields `nil` for most feeds, so `.scrub`/`unescapeHTML` crashes the entire scheduled job. No fallback to `i.description`/`i.content:encoded` and `String#scrub` requires Ruby >=2.1.

No handling for `rss` or `rss.items` being nil/empty.

Feed HTML/JS is persisted verbatim. Additionally `url` interpolation in `TopicEmbed.import` (`"#{url}"`) only checks prefix `^https?://` so `http://x/'>

`feed_key` is dead code: defined as `"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)}"` but never read, so conditional GET/If-Modified-Since caching is missing. Method would raise `TypeError` if `feed_polling_url` is nil. Consequently `poll_feed` re-fetches and re-imports every item hourly, doing redundant `TopicEmbed.where` + SHA comparisons and `PostRevisor` revisions even when feed unchanged, and partial failure leaves inconsistent state.

Throttle key uses two non-atomic commands: $redis.setnx then $redis.expire. If the process crashes between them the key is left without TTL and throttles that embed_url forever (permanent DoS for that URL). Should use atomic SET NX EX / SETEX.

Redis key is "retrieved:#{@embed_url}" with raw URL. Unbounded length, spaces/newlines/colons, no normalization or hashing. Allows redis memory bloat, key injection, and throttle bypass by trivial URL variations (trailing slash, encoding). Should hash the URL.

perform_retrieve synchronously polls the entire RSS/Atom feed on every single embed miss: Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) fetches and imports all items just to check if one embed_url exists. Adds latency, network failure surface, and O(feed_size) work per embed. Also guards only on feed_polling_enabled? while PollFeed requires feed_polling_url and embed_by_username, so it instantiates the poller even when it will no-op.

fetch_http does SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without nil/blank guard. SiteSetting.embed_by_username can be nil (stubbed as nil in poll_feed_spec and defaults to ''), raising NoMethodError: undefined method `downcase' for nil. PollFeed correctly checks .present? before downcasing. Here the job crashes instead of gracefully no-oping.

TopicEmbed.import_remote does open(url).read via open-uri with no timeout/rescue. Any HTTP error, timeout, DNS failure or Readability parse error bubbles out of perform_retrieve/retrieve unhandled, failing the Sidekiq job and causing retries that hammer the remote host. Concurrent misses also race past the exists? check and can hit the unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url raising RecordNotUnique with no rescue.

fetch_http does SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without presence guard. If setting is nil (or blank) this raises NoMethodError: undefined method `downcase' for nil. The scheduled job Jobs::PollFeed#execute guards with .present? before downcasing, but TopicRetriever does not, so a default/misconfigured forum crashes RetrieveTopic jobs. If blank string, lookup finds no user and silently returns nil with no error/log, leaving EmbedController in infinite 'loading' loop.

perform_retrieve synchronously runs Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) on every cache-miss (throttled only to 60s per URL). This imports the entire RSS feed, not just @embed_url, as a side-effect of a single embed request: wasteful, slow, and unexpectedly creates/updates many topics. The feed path has no rescue, so any OpenURI/SimpleRSS error (network failure, invalid RSS, i.content==nil causing CGI.unescapeHTML(nil.scrub) NoMethodError) propagates and prevents the fallback fetch_http from ever running.

fetch_http delegates to TopicEmbed.import_remote which does open(@embed_url).read with no timeout, size limit, or rescue. Any OpenURI::HTTPError/SocketError/Timeout/Errno error bubbles out of perform_retrieve/retrieve and fails the Jobs::RetrieveTopic Sidekiq job (no error handling/logging). The embed therefore never gets created and the frontend stays on loading with periodic retries, and the unhandled exception masks the root cause.

retrieved_recently? uses non-atomic $redis.setnx + $redis.expire. If the process crashes between the two, the key is left without TTL and throttles that embed_url forever. Should use SET with NX+EX atomically or ensure expire is set transactionally.

Direct interpolation of `url` into HTML `link = "#{url}"` without escaping. If url contains `'` or `>` it breaks out of the attribute and injects arbitrary HTML/JS. Because the resulting string is later stored with `cook_method: :raw_html` (bypassing sanitize) and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in embed view, this is a stored XSS. The URL regex on line 11 `^https?\:\/\/` also does not validate the remainder, so `http://' onerror` style URLs pass.

Creates post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` where `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim (no `post_analyzer.cook`/`Sanitize`). Combined with `contents` coming from RSS (`PollFeed` `i.content`) or `Readability::Document` with only a tag/attribute whitelist, arbitrary HTML (`<script>`, `onerror`, `javascript:` hrefs, `<iframe>`) is stored verbatim and later rendered unescaped in `embed/best.html.erb` via `raw post.cooked`. Enables stored XSS from any embeddable/RSS source.

Mutates caller's `contents` string in place with `contents << "\n<hr>..."`. Caller does not expect mutation; callers that reuse the string or retry will get double-appended footer, and if the string is frozen (e.g. frozen literal) it raises `RuntimeError: can't modify frozen String`. Should use `contents = contents + ...` or `dup`.

Checks `if post.present?` to decide whether to create `TopicEmbed`. `PostCreator#create` returns a `Post` object even on validation failure (unpersisted with errors), which is `present?`. This will attempt `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: nil, post_id: nil)` or with invalid ids, raising or creating orphaned embed, instead of checking `post.persisted?`/`post.errors.empty?` or `creator.errors`.

TOCTOU race: `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` is done outside `Topic.transaction` with no row lock (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`) or `find_or_create` handling. Concurrent `import` calls for same url can both see `embed.blank?` and both create a topic/post, violating the unique index on `embed_url` (raising `RecordNotUnique`) or creating duplicate topics.

SHA mismatch: `content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)` is computed *before* `absolutize_urls` is applied. The persisted `raw` is the absolutized form (`fragment.to_html`). SHA therefore does not represent stored content; relative vs absolute URLs are invisible to change detection. Also update path recomputes sha from pre-absolutized contents but compares/revises with absolutized raw, causing either missed updates or spurious revisions after sanitization/normalization.

contents << mutates caller's String in-place and interpolates url unsafely into HTML: "#{url}" without escaping. A crafted url like https://example.com/'> breaks out of the single-quoted href. Combined with cook_method :raw_html (Post#cook returns raw verbatim, bypassing sanitization, and embed view uses raw post.cooked), this is stored XSS. Mutation also causes double-appending if the same string object is reused (e.g., caller keeps reference) and will raise if contents is frozen.

Creation path checks `if post.present?` instead of `persisted?`/`errors.empty?`. PostCreator#create wraps save in Post.transaction and returns the Post object even after ActiveRecord::Rollback (e.g., has_host_spam? or validation failure - spam path raises Rollback but leaves @post with nil id/errors). present? is still true, so TopicEmbed.create! is attempted with nil topic_id/post_id violating NOT NULL and unique index, raising exception and leaving inconsistent state. Also check-then-create via `where(embed_url:).first` is racy: two concurrent imports can both see blank and hit unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url.

Update path is not atomic and mishandles failures: embed.post may be nil (deleted post) causing PostRevisor.new(nil) NoMethodError; revisor.revise! may return false (should_revise? or validation with skip_validations) yet embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...) still executes, desyncing sha from actual post raw. update_column bypasses validations/callbacks and is outside a transaction, so post updated but sha not, or vice versa, on crash. Should be wrapped in transaction and only update sha on successful revise.

content_sha1 is computed from contents before absolutize_urls, while raw stored in DB is after absolutize_urls (relative / URLs expanded). Future import computes sha from new pre-absolutized contents and compares to stored sha (also pre-absolutized), but post raw comparison in PostRevisor is on absolutized raw, causing divergence: identical feeds with different relative/absolute forms flip sha, and normal HTML serialization differences (Nokogiri to_html) cause unnecessary revisions every poll or miss real changes.

Unsafe Kernel#open on SiteSetting.feed_polling_url: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` delegates to Kernel.open patched by open-uri. If value starts with `|` it executes a shell command (classic Ruby open pipe RCE) and `file://` or internal http://169.254... allows SSRF/file disclosure. No scheme/host validation and no timeout. Should validate /^https?:\/\// and use URI.open/Net::HTTP with timeouts.

Nil crash on `i.content.scrub`: many RSS/Atom feeds provide `description` not `content:encoded`, so SimpleRSS `i.content` is nil. `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole hourly job (retry:false). Same for `rss` being `false`/`nil` on parse failure then `rss.items` raises. Need `i.content || i.description || ""` and guard `rss && rss.items`.

Stored XSS via raw_html bypass: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` is passed straight to `TopicEmbed.import` which creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` un-sanitized, later rendered with `raw post.cooked` in embed view. Unlike `import_remote` which whitelists tags/attributes via Readability, the RSS path allows arbitrary `<script>`, `<iframe onload=>`, etc. from external feed.

Unrescued network/parse exceptions kill scheduled job: `open` can raise OpenURI::HTTPError/SocketError/Timeout::Error/URI::InvalidURIError and `SimpleRSS.parse` can return false or raise. No rescue. With `sidekiq_options retry:false` the hourly PollFeed fails silently until next hour with no logging or error handling, and one bad feed blocks processing of all items.

Dead/buggy `feed_key`: method is defined and memoized via `@feed_key ||=` but never read anywhere (no Redis If-Modified-Since/ETag handling). Memoization makes it stale if `feed_polling_url` changes during process lifetime, and `Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(nil)` would raise TypeError if called when setting blank. Indicates incomplete conditional-fetch optimization.

Resource leak: `SimpleRSS.parse open(url)` uses non-block form of open-uri, leaving the returned Tempfile/StringIO open until GC. Should use block form `open(url){|f| SimpleRSS.parse(f)}` or `open(url).read` / `URI.open` to ensure close.

open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) has no error handling, timeout, SSRF validation or pipe-sanitization. OpenURI::HTTPError/SocketError, invalid XML, or a URL beginning with '|' (Kernel.open pipe injection) raises unrescued exception, and with sidekiq_options retry:false the hourly job just dies. SimpleRSS.parse can return false on bad XML so rss.items then raises NoMethodError.

Nil.scrub raises NoMethodError and aborts entire poll_feed loop. No fallback to i.description and no nil-guard. Same for i.title possibly nil.

RSS HTML is passed unsanitized to TopicEmbed.import which stores with cook_method :raw_html and bypasses markdown/sanitize (Post#cook returns raw). Rendered via `raw post.cooked` in embed/best.html.erb => stored XSS if feed is compromised.

Intended conditional GET / If-Modified-Since / de-duplication is dead code, so poll_feed unconditionally fetches and re-iterates every item hourly. Also key hashes the URL itself, not content/ETag/Last-Modified, so even if wired would never change.

import_remote does `open(url).read` without `require 'open-uri'`, without URL validation, timeout or exception handling. If open-uri not loaded, Kernel#open treats http URL as file path and fails; with open-uri it still allows SSRF/command-injection via pipe (`open("| cmd")`) because validation (`^https?://`) happens only later in `import`, after the fetch. Unhandled OpenURI::HTTPError/SocketError/URI::InvalidURIError will crash RetrieveTopic/PollFeed jobs.

This breaks links and, combined with raw_html rendering, leaves XSS vectors.

Even with open-uri, it fetches any URL without SSRF protection (follows redirects, can reach internal/metadata IPs, file:// if host check bypassed) and raises unhandled exceptions on network/timeout/invalid URI, crashing the job.

Content imported via readability and especially via PollFeed (which bypasses readability) is stored with Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] (Post#cook returns raw verbatim). Needs locking/`find_or_create` with rescue/retry.

response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL" is not a valid X-Frame-Options directive (valid are DENY, SAMEORIGIN, ALLOW-FROM). Browsers ignore unknown values and may default to DENY/SAMEORIGIN, so legitimate embeds will remain blocked. To allow framing from the embeddable_host the header should be removed (or set to ALLOW-FROM). The helper also caches headers via AnonymousCache, so the invalid value gets cached.

ensure_embeddable authorizes solely on URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host. Referer is a client-controlled header trivially spoofed with curl, so it is not an access control. It also breaks when browsers suppress Referer (Referrer-Policy: no-referrer) as URI('').host is nil != host, denying legitimate iframe loads. No check of params[:embed_url] host is done here; authorization is deferred to async TopicRetriever.

params.require(:embed_url) is used unvalidated (no URL format/host allowlist) and directly used for TopicEmbed lookup, Jobs.enqueue, and anon cache key (REQUEST_URI). An attacker can enqueue arbitrary embed_url values (including arrays => WHERE embed_url IN (...), or paths with query/credentials) causing Sidekiq flood/SSRF to embeddable_host, cache-key explosion/pollution, and stale cache: discourse_expires_in caches the 'loading' response for 1 minute via AnonymousCache (key = host+uri) so after the topic is created anonymous users still get the cached loading page until expiry.

X-Frame-Options "ALLOWALL" is not a valid directive (valid values are DENY, SAMEORIGIN, ALLOW-FROM). Browsers treat an invalid value as DENY/SAMEORIGIN or ignore it, so the iframe will be blocked despite the controller intending to allow framing. Correct fix is to delete the header (response.headers.delete('X-Frame-Options')) or set CSP frame-ancestors. Spec at spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:37 asserts the invalid value, so test enforces the bug.
