When limit is reached, a new device correctly gets this error, but an existing device whose updated_at is older than 30d (expired, not counted by CountDevices) also gets ErrDeviceLimitReached. Caller in client.go treats this as limit-reached and denies anonymous authentication (return nil, err), so stale-device re-activation is denied and error is mis-reported.

casa.which: 7 (defect 2 describes the identical same cause/consequence - RowsAffected==0 due to updated_at >30d window conflated with ErrDeviceLimitReached, denying update of existing stale device when limit reached; i.e. 2 and 7 are duplicates of the comment)

achados.description: Test only verifies the rejection path (new device_id -> ErrDeviceLimitReached) but does not verify the complementary allowed path: updating an existing device when count >= limit must succeed. The PR's logic in database.go:115-116 is "if limit reached, only updates" via updateDevice(). This test would still pass if updateDevice were broken and always returned ErrDeviceLimitReached, so it does not check the claimed contract and gives false coverage.

Device literal omits CreatedAt (leaves zero time 0001-01-01) while production TagDevice in impl.go always sets CreatedAt=UpdatedAt=time.Now(). The inserted row is therefore unrealistic; SQLite accepts it but Postgres/MySQL timestamp handling/NOT NULL defaults differ, and CreatedAt handling bugs are masked.

Reuses the same *Device pointer and mutates DeviceID/UpdatedAt in place for the second call instead of creating a new Device struct. This aliasing loses the original reference, prevents asserting DB state after success/failure (count remains 1, original row unchanged), and implicitly reuses stale ClientIP/UserAgent, making the test confusing and incomplete.

Test reuses same *Device and only checks error for new ID, without verifying DB state. It never asserts CountDevices/ListDevices remains 1 or that no second row was inserted. So it would pass even if CreateOrUpdateDevice incorrectly inserted and then returned error, giving false confidence that limit is enforced.

CreatedAt is left as zero value and UpdatedAt is set to time.Now().Add(-1h), unlike production in anonimpl/impl.go:136-141 which uses time.Now() for both. The PR's database.go:110 counts with time.Now() window but database.go:81 updateDevice filters with device.UpdatedAt window; using stale -1h hides the mismatch and hides the bug that an existing but expired (>30d) device would fail the BETWEEN check and incorrectly return ErrDeviceLimitReached even for an allowed update.

Test only covers the error path (new device when limit reached) and never tests the success path required by database.go:115-116 comment 'only update devices' — i.e., that updating an existing device_id when count >= limit should succeed via updateDevice. Missing coverage hides that client.go:45-46 now turns ErrDeviceLimitReached into `return nil, err` denying anonymous authentication entirely, so limit becomes a DoS for all new anonymous users with no test for the allowed existing-device refresh.

tagDeviceUI inserts into localCache BEFORE CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds (impl.go:87 SetDefault before 93). TagDevice now propagates ErrDeviceLimitReached (144-148 return err). First over-limit request correctly returns ErrDeviceLimitReached and Authenticate fails, but the failed deviceID is already cached for 29m. Next request for same deviceID hits cache (83-84) and returns nil, bypassing the limit. Transient DB errors are also cached and suppress retries for 29 minutes. This is cache-poisoning that lets limit be bypassed via retry and hides errors.

ClientIP handling is wrong order and dead: clientIPStr := ip.String() is executed before len(ip)==0 check, so a nil/empty net.IP yields string "<nil>" stored in DB instead of "". The len check after String() is dead code (err already checked, ip is non-nil on success). Exposed now because TagDevice changed from async fire-and-forget to synchronous return err, so bogus IPs are now persisted synchronously on the auth path.

TagDevice now does synchronous DB work and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached to Authenticate (client.go:44-46 returns nil, err). Previously tagging was async in a goroutine with context.WithTimeout(2m) and panic recovery, not blocking login. Now every anonymous Authenticate blocks on CountDevices + Create/Update using the request ctx with no timeout, adding DB latency to auth hot path (DoS/timeout risk) and turning a soft limit into hard auth failure (nil Identity + error -> 401/500 for all new anon devices, no graceful 429 or allow-auth-but-not-count).

Poisoned localCache bypasses device limit. tagDeviceUI does Get/SetDefault before CreateOrUpdateDevice. When s.deviceLimit is reached CreateOrUpdateDevice calls updateDevice which returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for unknown deviceID (0 rows). TagDevice now returns that error (133-148 return err) so first request is denied. But the cache entry was already set, so second request for same new deviceID within 29m hits `if _,ok:=a.localCache.Get(key); ok {return nil}` and TagDevice returns nil, letting Authenticate succeed. Limit is enforced only once per cache TTL. Same for any transient DB error: cache prevents retry.

Sync blocking on hot auth path + availability gate. Before: go func() with context.Background timeout 2m + recover, best-effort, never failed Authenticate. After: TagDevice is called synchronously on request ctx and TagDevice propagates error. Every anonymous login now pays CountDevices+Write latency; ctx cancel/timeout or DB slowness blocks auth. Combined with `return err` in TagDevice, any DB/count error (including ErrDeviceLimitReached) is surfaced to Anonymous.Authenticate which now denies anonymous login (returns nil,err) turning telemetry into hard auth gate.

Error contract broken / double logging. Service.TagDevice previously always returned nil (swallowed errors). Region now returns err, but client.go only treats ErrDeviceLimitReached as fatal (return nil,err), other errors are just Warn-logged and auth still succeeds. So TagDevice returning generic DB errors is useless work and causes duplicate logs (impl.go Debug + client.go Warn) and changes interface semantics without updating callers/tests.

Time-window and stale-device denial. updateDevice does `UPDATE ... WHERE device_id=? AND updated_at BETWEEN now-30d AND now+1m` using the new device.UpdatedAt (=time.Now()) as both bound and value. An existing device that hasn't been seen for >30d or whose stored updated_at is slightly in future (>1m skew) affects 0 rows and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, which TagDevice propagates as auth denial, even though CountDevices excludes that stale device and it should be allowed to re-register.

TOCTOU race with no transaction. CreateOrUpdateDevice checks `count >= s.deviceLimit` then either INSERT or UPDATE. Concurrent TagDevice calls (now synchronous per request) can both see count < limit and both INSERT, exceeding limit. No SELECT FOR UPDATE / unique constraint guard on count, so limit is not enforceable under concurrency.

anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined lacks explicit type annotation. GrafanaConfig defines it as `number | undefined` (packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200) so the class field must be `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined`. With bare `= undefined` the inferred type is `undefined` only, breaking the implements contract and hiding type errors; `merge(this,defaults,options)` then assigns a number at runtime to a property statically typed as undefined (type unsoundness). Follow existing typed pattern.

Default/contract mismatch with backend. Go side defaults to 0 = unlimited (pkg/setting/setting.go:374 init 0, pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go:195 `int64` `json:"anonymousDeviceLimit"` always serializes 0) while frontend GrafanaConfig types it as `number | undefined` and defaults to `undefined`. Runtime after `merge` gets 0, but code/tests that check `!== undefined` will misinterpret 0 (unlimited) as a limit, and initial `undefined` state leaks before bootData merge. DTO should be *int64 omitempty or frontend type should be `number` with consistent 0 semantics.

Field declared as `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined` without explicit type. Inferred type is `undefined` literal, not `number | undefined` as required by `GrafanaConfig` (packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200). With `implements GrafanaConfig` this is a type error under strict checks; later `merge(this, defaults, options)` (lodash, `any`) hides it. Should be `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined` (or explicit `number`).

Contract mismatch + information leak. Frontend type is `number | undefined` with default `undefined` meaning "no limit", but `FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit int64` (no `omitempty`) always serializes as `0` for unlimited (pkg/setting/setting.go:1654 MustInt64(0), pkg/api/frontendsettings.go:198). After boot `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` becomes `0` not `undefined`, so checks for `undefined` vs `0` diverge. Limit is also exposed unauthenticated via `/api/frontend/settings` (getFrontendSettings) leaking server-side capacity controls.

DI breakage linked to new config. `ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore db.DB, deviceLimit int64)` now requires `int64`, but `pkg/server/wire.go:374` still registers `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` in `wireBasicSet` without any binding for `int64` – wire generation / compilation fails. `anonimpl.ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:43) works around by manually calling `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit)` instead of injecting `AnonStore`, leaving the wire-provided `AnonStore` orphaned/duplicate.

Limit enforcement introduces synchronous auth denial. Previous `client.go:Authenticate` tagged device in fire-and-forget goroutine (best-effort, 2m timeout). Now it does `TagDevice(ctx,...)` synchronously and on `ErrDeviceLimitReached` returns `nil, err`, denying anonymous login and blocking the auth path on DB `CountDevices`+`updateDevice` latency. `updateDevice` uses `UPDATE ... WHERE device_id=? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?` and returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` on `RowsAffected==0`, so any *new* device when at limit is rejected (intended) but also an existing device whose `updated_at` is outside the `anonymousDeviceExpiration` window cannot be re-added – count excludes expired rows but update still fails, cause indefinite denial. Race between concurrent `CountDevices` and inserts also allows limit bypass.

getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when modelSupplier.get() == null (concurrent delete). This violates GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() contract which is documented @return Never returns null and default impl returns count. Callers like GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount() do representation.setSubGroupCount(group.getSubGroupsCount()) and may unbox to long, causing NPE/type violation downstream. Correct behavior for deleted/unknown group should be 0L, empty stream, or IllegalStateException (as isUpdated() does), not null.

Fix is incomplete/inconsistent: the three getSubGroupsStream(..) overloads still do return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) with no null-check. Under the same concurrent-delete race that motivated the getSubGroupsCount null-guard, they will throw NPE (modelSupplier.get() == null) instead of handling deletion gracefully, so the NPE is only moved from count to stream methods.

Uses LazyModel (caches first result) for the null-check. If the first modelSupplier.get() succeeds, the model is cached and later concurrent deletion is invisible — getSubGroupsCount() will return stale count instead of noticing deletion. Conversely if first call is after deletion, null is returned. Combined with isUpdated() branch which throws IllegalStateException on not-found after invalidation, the same deleted state yields two different outcomes (exception vs null vs stale value) depending on timing/cache.

Added test createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti never joins the reader thread. It sets deletedAll=true and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty. The reader loop may still be inside managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...) or about to do another iteration; exceptions thrown after the assert are missed, and the thread leaks. Need Thread.join (with timeout) / Executor and await termination before assertion, otherwise test is flaky and does not actually verify absence of exceptions.

getSubGroupsCount() now returns `null` when `modelSupplier.get()==null` (concurrent delete). This violates GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() contract (`@return Never returns null`, default impl returns count) and breaks callers like GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount/representation.setSubGroupCount which expect non-null Long. Unboxing or arithmetic on the result will NPE later; hiding the race with null is wrong — should return 0L (or fall back to cached empty) and be consistent with isUpdated() path which throws IllegalStateException.

Incomplete race fix: the three getSubGroupsStream* delegates on lines 256, 262, 268 still do `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` without null-check. Under the same concurrent delete that motivated the getSubGroupsCount null-guard they throw NullPointerException, so the PR claims to prevent NPE on concurrent read/delete but leaves 3 of 4 delegation paths vulnerable. Fix must null-guard all or return Stream.empty()/0.

Test does not verify what it claims and is racy/flaky: reader thread is fire-and-forget with no join/await before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty())`, so assertion can run before loop body executes or before exception is added (false pass). Busy while(!deletedAll) with no backoff/join is non-deterministic and does not assert subGroupCount semantics (null vs 0) nor that briefRepresentation count path was exercised, masking defect #1.

Reader thread is started but never joined/awaited. `deletedAll.set(true)` is followed immediately by `assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty())` while the background thread may still be in-flight inside `groups(...)`. Any exception added after the assertion is missed (false-negative → test passes even if NPE/ IllegalStateException still occurs) and the thread leaks beyond the test method contaminating subsequent tests / leaving orphan HTTP calls.

Busy-spin `while (!deletedAll.get()) { groups(null,0,Integer.MAX_VALUE,true); }` with no sleep/yield/backoff and with `max=Integer.MAX_VALUE` hammers the server with repeated full-list fetches. Causes unbounded CPU/load, risk of OOM from huge payload, and flaky timing.

No coordination to guarantee concurrency window. `new Thread(...).start()` is asynchronous and deletions run sequentially immediately after; deletions of 100 groups can finish before the reader performs its first request. Test therefore often exercises no overlap at all and does not reliably verify the `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount` null-model race it claims to cover, giving false confidence. Missing latch/barrier to ensure overlapping execution.

Reader thread is started with new Thread(...).start() but never joined/awaited before assertThat. deletedAll.set(true) is set and the assertion runs immediately while the thread may still be in-flight. An exception added after the assertion is missed (false positive) and the thread leaks beyond the test method, hammering the server during subsequent tests. Correct harness must join with timeout.

Busy spin while(!deletedAll.get()) with no sleep/backoff or timeout. Tight loop floods //admin/groups (Integer.MAX_VALUE) concurrently with deletes, makes test flaky/resource-heavy, masks the real race window, and can hang forever if delete loop throws before deletedAll is set. Needs throttling and timeout.

Test claims to verify concurrent read+delete does not throw (NPE from GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount), but only checks caughtExceptions is empty at a racily-observed instant. Because there is no join, and because GroupAdapter now returns null violating GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() 'Never returns null' contract, the test does not verify representation correctness (null subGroupCount) and can pass while server still violates contract / other getSubGroupsStream overloads still NPE. Assertion does not actually prove the fix.

Reader thread is started but never joined/awaited. DeletedAll is set to true and assert is executed immediately without happens-before with thread termination. Exceptions occurring after the assert or still-in-flight requests are missed (false pass) and the thread leaks beyond the test method, polluting subsequent tests.

Assertion assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty()) races with the reader thread. It can be evaluated before the reader has performed any concurrent read during deletes or before it observes deletedAll, so test can pass even if concurrent getSubGroupsCount would throw NPE/500. No Thread.join(timeout) or await.

Shares managedRealm.admin() / underlying JAX-RS admin client across two concurrent threads. Admin client / RESTEasy proxy is not documented as thread-safe; concurrent use can cause connection/ token race failures or mask the server-side race the test intends to reproduce.

Busy spin while(!deletedAll.get()) with no sleep/backoff, no timeout and no guaranteed termination. If group removal throws or deletedAll never set, the thread loops forever and the test hangs. Non-daemon thread will outlive the test.

Test checks only that client did not throw (caughtExceptions empty) and never asserts the contract the PR fixes: GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() must never return null. The fix in GroupAdapter returns null when modelSupplier.get()==null, violating @return Never returns null and causing GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount -> representation.setSubGroupCount(null) / potential NPE on unboxing. Test would still pass.

Uses groups(null,0,Integer.MAX_VALUE,true) (briefRepresentation=true) in tight loop without verifying response content. It does not assert subGroupCount presence/non-null, so NPE postponed to server inside GroupUtils/ModelToRepresentation would surface as HTTP 500 which is caught, but null-return path is not explicitly validated; test does not check what it claims to protect (concurrent getSubGroupsCount).

getSubGroupsCount now returns `null` when modelSupplier.get()==null. GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() is documented `Never returns null` (GroupModel.java:298, default impl returns count()). JPA impl always returns 0..n. Callers like GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount / ModelToRepresentation expect non-null (autounboxing, JSON) and will NPE or propagate null subGroupCount. Should return 0L or delegate correctly, not null.

Reader thread is started and never joined before asserting `assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty())`. Assertion is racy: thread can add exception after the check, so test can pass while concurrent request failed. Thread also leaks beyond test method, can outlive ManagedRealm cleanup and pollute following tests; no join/timeout/interrupt handling.

Fix is inconsistent: getSubGroupsCount is null-guarded but sibling methods getSubGroupsStream(search,first,max), getSubGroupsStream(first,max), getSubGroupsStream(search,exact,first,max) do `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` without null check (lines 256,262,268). Same concurrent delete race that motivated the fix still throws NPE on those paths. Test gives false confidence by only exercising the briefRepresentations path.

Busy spin `while(!deletedAll.get())` with no sleep/backoff, no stored Thread handle, not daemon, no interrupt. If delete loop throws or test fails, deletedAll never becomes true and thread spins forever consuming CPU. Tight loop also starves server and makes test flaky/non-deterministic; does not actually verify what it claims beyond 'no exception seen at one instant'.
